#4290. Nekome: Nazi Hunter Director On Whether The Game Is Political, Art Inspiration, Metaphysical Themes, Steam Demo, And More

I've been tracking Nekome: Nazi Hunter here at Game Informer since its reveal earlier this year. I finally went hands-on with it during Gamescom 2026 and relished just how disrespectfully brutal it is to Nazis. You will soon get the chance to experience that brutality yourself because developer ProbablyMonsters is releasing a demo on Steam soon on October 19, and it will be available through October 26.

Ahead of that demo launch, ProbablyMonsters also released a new trailer highlighting the game's narrative and villainous Hyena troupe of Nazi leaders as part of today's Galaxies Autumn Showcase. These Hyenas are at the center of protagonist Vano's Nazi hunting, and they are a notorious squad of Nazi agents whose extreme brand of cruelty made them feared across occupied Europe and the world, according to a press release. Players will control Vano as he kills countless Nazis in violent and bloody ways while tracking down each of the Hyenas (who he will presumably also kill violently and bloodily).

Check it out in the latest Nekome: Nazi Hunter trailer for yourself below:

Game Informer also spoke to Nekome: Nazi Hunter game director Jeronimo Barrera about the game in the lead-up to this trailer and the incoming Steam Next Fest demo. In the interview, which took place over email, Barrera talks about the game's politics (or lack thereof), the Hyenas, visual inspiration, and more:

Game Informer's Wesley LeBlanc: How did the team decide on the Hyenas as the antagonists/villains of the game, rather than say, the obvious choice of Hitler?

Barrera: As we developed the narrative, we had already committed to pursuing the grindhouse aesthetic that would drive the presentation. We needed a disgusting set of villains that would be fun to hunt down and murder. Although we are rooted in real-world events, the player fantasy we are after is to hunt down and murder as many Nazis, both big and small, and that needs to deliver over-the-top fun.

Can you tell me about the Hyenas? What are their differences from a narrative perspective, and what are their differences from a gameplay perspective? Does each Hyena approach the hunt for Vano in different ways?

We introduce the Hyenas almost immediately in the narrative. After that, the player won’t be confused as to why they need to hunt them down, not the other way around! Vano hunts them down, and each Hyena boss fight is a unique challenge that pushes the players' abilities.

It sounds like Vano will be hunted across occupied Europe and beyond? What can you tell me about that beyond?

Our research into how we can tell a new story and give a new experience has given us a lot of surprising locations to explore. For example, we were shocked when we realized that we could have our first encounters with Nazis on U.S. soil! Vano’s adopted home is New York City. It’s hard to believe, but there were Nazi Party rallies in New York. This is where Vano starts his hunt through a tragic coincidence, which then takes Vano to Europe. But he’s not being hunted; he is the hunter.

Is there anything larger than life or supernatural or demonic happening narratively, or is it Vano versus some Nazis that are led by the Hyenas? I ask because scenes in this new trailer almost imply some monstrous transformation, or maybe even something vampiric, as blood drips from the Hyenas' faces (though I recognize that could just be a style choice).

The Nazis were hideous monsters. We play on those themes for our abilities and how we present them to the player. There are themes we explore that could be considered metaphysical. But with that said, it’s up for people to interpret the narrative on their own.

How would you describe the art style/visual design of the game?

Our biggest inspiration came from the grindhouse film genre. Turning the stylized pulpiness and violence of movies like Inglourious Basterds into a video game was a challenge that the team was excited to tackle, and we believe this grindhouse spirit gives our game a distinct visual style.

Graphic novels were another major influence. Our goal with the art style was to create something over the top and entertaining, while respecting the serious subject matter. The game would lose its sense of fun if it looked too real, and graphic novels helped us find a look that is visually interesting yet able to handle the story’s darkness and violence.

How long has the team been working on the game?

The team began working on the game in 2024. The genesis of the game was a meeting inside ProbablyMonsters where we started quoting Inglourious Basterds, and we all became set on the idea of making a game about hunting down and killing Nazis through an untold Second World War story.

Nekome: Nazi Hunter’s development is led internally at ProbablyMonsters by Brett Bourbin, Brand Inman, Sergei Kuprejanov, Kay Willis and me, with assistance from co-development partners.

What has it been like working on a smaller title like this and what does your AAA experience bring to the project?

Going from concept to the player’s hands in 18 months is an epic lift that’s only possible with amazing devs that bring extraordinary experience and expertise. The AAA sensibilities run deep at ProbablyMonsters; there are some legends in our house. What makes us different is that our independent approach allows us to tell unique stories and make experiences like Nekome that would have a hard time getting to market.

After Gamescom, ButWhyTho? published a story about how Willis said the game isn’t political, and it caused a lot of discussion/backlash about the game. I wanted to see if the team had any follow-up on the idea that Nekome isn’t political now that some time has passed. At least from my perspective, all art is political; not to mention, making a game where you’re very much visibly and graphically killing and mutilating Nazis is sending a very clear message, especially in 2026 when we have people proudly stating they are a Nazi today. But that’s just my line of thinking – I’m curious where the team lands on this discussion now that some additional time has passed.

I think we're overcomplicating this. Nazis are bad. That shouldn't be a political statement, just common sense. Nekome is a revenge story about people who suffered horrific atrocities at the hands of Nazis. We're not making a statement about modern politics. We're telling a story with villains who are unquestionably evil.

If someone feels politically attacked by a game where you kill Nazis, maybe they should take a long, hard look in the mirror.

Anything I missed you’d like to touch on?

We created Nekome because we saw an opportunity to tell a Second World War story through a perspective that games have rarely depicted. World War II is one of the most common settings in media. And yet, there are almost no games that explore the persecution of the Roma and Sinti during that period.

That is a real, deeply horrible part of history, so our story also comes with responsibility. The team has worked with historians and cultural consultants to help us approach Vano’s identity, his community and the historical context thoughtfully and credibly. We promise to tell Vano’s story honestly and approach that history with care.

The story follows the Proxies getting invited backstage to support the group, which also includes helping them set up practice schedules, organise events and manage social media activities. There’s a rhythm minigame as part of that, along with new maps and mechanics for Marcel Adventure.

Angels of Delusion is also the group that the two new Agents being introduced in this update belong to. Members of the same group are capable of performing coordinated attacks. The new arrivals are Sunna and Aria.

Sunna is a an S-Rank Physical Support Agent who specialises in boosting teammates using Attack and Anomaly. Her Ultimate sees her pull out a giant hammer to land heavy damage, and bring teammates into combat using Quick Assist. Sunna’s companion, Bubblegum, can cast Cat's Gaze on enemies, marking them for detonation. Bubblegum can also buff the squad’s attack.

Aria is the other new arrival, the group’s lead vocalist who can shift between two forms, idol projection and construct. Aria is an Ether Anomaly Agent who also deals high burst damage, specifically against enemies who suffer from any Attribute Anomalies.

Sunna and Aria also benefit from the support of the amusingly named Bangboo Biggest Fan, a fan club president who can heal them over time, and boost the squad’s Attack any time two or more Angels of Delusion members are present.

Version 2.6’s S-Rank re-runs are Yixuan (Auric Ink - Rupture), and Yuzuha (Physical - Support), who you can look forward to as part of the banners.

Version 2.6 will also expand Hollow Zero with a new game mode, Operation Matrix. The mode offers themed stages that rotate weekly, each offering new mechanics. You can now also Sweep in Hollow Zero.

Beyond all the celebrations, this update also brings combat kit overhauls to a couple of older S-Rank characters, Lycaon and Harumasa. You can look forward to multiple limited-time events, too, including one where you can earn a new outfit for Pan Yinhu.

The big event is naturally going to be themed around Gilded Carrot Day, and it actually starts today. There’s the usual run of login rewards (about 3,300 Polychromes), as well as daily activities. Yet another login event - Gilded Surprise, Wonderful Boo-ns - will be available February 14-23, offering daily draws from a pool of 4 billion Polychrome.

#4286. Eternal Anima Hands-On Preview – Strive How I Want To

Eternal Anima is the time-twisting RPG revealed during the big September Nintendo Direct that looked like a Square Enix HD-2D game but isn’t. It is also the game with the “Never Strive For A Better Tomorrow” splash screen. After playing the game for roughly an hour within developer Marvelous Inc.’s Tokyo office, I eschew that line – I will, in fact, strive for a better tomorrow, if only so I can play more Eternal Anima one day.

The world has essentially come to its final act in Eternal Anima. Urvis Ael is the last remaining bastion of civilization in a flooded world. That said, living in Urvis Ael isn’t all that bad; just don’t strive for a better tomorrow or really any kind of change. Protagonist Wade breaks those rules and sets out on an adventure, feeling deep down that a better life is possible.

Wade is bestowed with the power of Psychometry, which lets him look into the past, view memories, and inherit abilities and classes for use in combat. My hands-on time with Eternal Anima is mostly focused on combat, and for good reason: it rules. It is turn-based combat, but with a time-turning twist. Wade also has the power of Future Sight, which means he already knows exactly what every enemy will do each turn, reflected in the UI. Every ability has an action speed shown on the timeline at the bottom of the screen. You can always see an enemy’s upcoming action, who they will target, and even the outcome.

Combat in Eternal Anima is less about hitting enemies harder and more about hitting them smarter. When you attack an enemy's weaknesses with Wade or other party members, you knock them back on the battle timeline, pushing their predecided actions back in the move queue. Your goal is to push them back enough that you kill them before they can attack, or, for bigger enemies, knock them off the timeline in what’s known as a Break. This cancels their action, opening up your party for another round of attacks.

The battle system doesn’t feel as active as a standard turn-based RPG; instead, it makes you feel more like a god playing with action figures. You decide what happens, then sit back and watch it all unfold.

Everything is depicted in a beautiful, bokeh-enhanced art style that’s unique to Eternal Anima, despite the initial HD-2D impression. I love how the world and enemies look, which makes it even more disappointing that the characters are rendered as chibi. It doesn’t gel with the game’s painterly visuals and clashes with its heavier thematic tones.

As I explore Eternal Anima’s miniature settings, which resemble closed-off dioramas placed carefully on a larger world map, I take part in fishing minigames, collect items, defeat enemies, and encounter NPCs from the past, like Fletcher. After I interact with a glowing sword on the ground, an animated flashback plays, detailing Fletcher’s story and ending with a notification that I received a bow from his past.

As I continue through this world, some two centuries before my time, I encounter a man from this period who’s trying to save his forest hometown from flooding. Of course, I already know this will happen in my timeline because the entire world is flooded, but Wade suspects that if he can convince this person of the looming threat, he can change the present by altering the past. My demo ends shortly after, but now, a month removed from the preview, I’m still thinking about Eternal Anima, specifically its combat.

A lot of turn-based combat makes you feel powerful. But Eternal Anima’s makes you feel like a genius, and that’s smart and novel. I’m left striving for March now.

#4285. 10 Street Fighter Movie Changes That Could Completely Divide Longtime Fans

Some of the response to the recent Street Fighter movie hasn't been the most friendly. When you go into an adaptation like this, that's always a risk, but I'll be honest: I really liked it! It was just the right mix of fun, stupid, and unserious that it hit right for me. We got spectacle, some funny moments, and an easy watch.

With a crushing low from reviewers, the newest Street Fighter film has been compared to Morbius after some baffling creative decisions.

That said, the movie made some pretty big, sweeping changes that made me think, "Wait a minute..." While I don't think these changes are so big or bad that they've ruined it, I can totally see why they can completely divide longtime franchise fans. Especially since Street Fighter is one of Capcom's best franchises.

In the movie, Dan Hibiki is Ken's manager, friend, and a generally comical character. There's barely any hint that he has martial arts skills until near the end of the movie, where he fails to do anything particularly useful.

I'm not saying this is necessarily bad, but in the games he was a playable fighter with a little more to him than simple comedy. I think reframing his entire character as Ken's comic sidekick isn't the best move, but I do appreciate the relationship that unfolds on screen. There were a few hints about his game characterization and history, so it's not that bad, but it still stood out to me.

Bison has what I'll euphemistically call a colorful characterization in the 2026 Street Fighter movie. He's still a ruthless authoritarian dictator with massive ambitions, but he also comes with a foot fetish and a bizarrely sexualized approach that spills over whenever he interacts with quite a few of the main cast members.

I'm no prude, but this particular fixation just seems weird and pretty unnecessary given the wider context. It almost overshadows the genuinely menacing bits of his characterization and makes him into a comic figure. I feel like the film almost reduces him to this more comical aspect, and that's definitely not going to be universally popular.

One of the cool things about a movie adaptation like this one is that you get to see a lot of fan-favorite characters rendered in live action, with glorious costumes and genuine characterization. It's almost the entire point of something like this, even if sometimes we do get nervous.

Some video game stories are praised as masterpieces but these ten are certainly not worth the hype.

With Street Fighter, though, a lot of the iconic fighters aren't all that developed at all. Some are background characters, some have a few lines or a short fight sequence, but most don't get much meaningful screen time. This is genuinely difficult to manage with a cast this large, so I do get it, but it feels like a tick-box exercise rather than a meaningful inclusion.

I know that when you adapt something like this, you have to craft a real story. Good writing needs all sorts of things, from strong motivations, character relationships, conflict, all that good stuff. I know that it's a bit harder to pull that off when the story revolves around a fighting tournament.

A fighting game movie is different from a fighting game. But this one barely features the tournament at all, which feels like a misstep for me. One of the big draws of Street Fighter is the fighting; despite the action sequences, I didn't feel like there was an awful lot of iconic Street Fighter-style moments in the movie. Maybe I'm just picky, but I would have liked to have seen some more of the tournament itself.

I'm not sure how I feel about this moment. On the one hand, this is a class movie trope, and it feels appropriately pulpy: when Ryu is Dark Ryu during the climax, Ken fires off a Flaming Hadouken to stop him, then plays him his favorite song — 4 Non Blondes's What's Up.

We've got gods and demons throwing hands in the streets.

On the other hand, I'm not sure if it really feels quite right. It almost trivializes Ryu's struggle against the Satsui no Hado, even though it's pretty nice that his long-time friend and rival Ken is the one to help him. It feels almost comedic, which isn't quite right emotional tone in my opinion.

In the game canon, Ryu is a traveling fighter who roams the world training intensively to become a true martial artist; his pursuit of this is his core identity. In the movie, Ryu gives up martial arts to become a homeless ramen vendor.

I understand that the ramen diversion is a visual shorthand for Ryu's internal struggle and showcases how it's upended his life, but this is a fairly massive departure from his characterization as a dedicated martial artist. I get what it's trying to do, but I can also see why it would be divisive, even if he does eventually go back to fighting.

In the games, Ken was always established as a wealthy martial artist, but he was treated as a serious fighter. The movie turns him into a celebrity martial artist who makes money from brand deals and stunt appearances, such as fighting a "polar bear" (which was really just a man in a suit).

This is one of those movie moments that helps create a distinct character with his own motivations, but it shifts his tone from a dedicated, elite fighter to a commercial spectacle. It all works out in the end, and we see that Ken is actually a good fighter, but it seems like a weird diversion.

Cammy's game character was formerly associated with Bison's Dolls, but had been rescued and fought against him. In the movie, she's part of his group, and dutifully pursues the heroes and attempts to capture them.

I don't think this one is totally egregious, since I think it could be an attempt to showcase her character arc in future sequels, turning her from a loyal Bison operative into their opponent. Still, since we've only got the first movie to go on, this is one of those details that could go either way. I think it's interesting to see the character at a different point in her arc, but I can see why some fans might prefer a different depiction.

In the games, Ryu and Ken are described as being close friends and closer rivals. Their competition is tightly woven into their relationship, but in a more positive way. They build on each other's successes rather than take delight in each other's deficiencies. In the movie, Ryu sabotages Ken by destroying his invitation to the first World Warrior Tournament out of jealousy.

I respect what they're doing here, because it gives Ryu an underlying insecurity and darkness that helps ground his storyline, but it does make their relationship feel tonally different in a way that might not go down well with long-time fans.

Obviously, adaptations don't need to follow the original continuity, especially if they're telling a completely new story. This one seems to make Gouken's death permanent: Akuma murders Gouken after the World Warrior Tournament, which causes Ryu to withdraw from the world.

In the game canon, Gouken is revealed to survive. They could still pull this one off in the movie continuity, but it did look pretty conclusive that he'd died. It's not just about him dying early, though: his death changes the foundation of Ryu and Ken's story and relationship. It's easy to see why long-time fans might not be too pleased with how everything's turned out.

These are the games that didn't get invited to prom, but ended up being pretty cool regardless of how popular they were.

#4283. d4v41 and Jinggg leave Paper Rex after 7th–8th Champions finish, Pacific place secure

Paper Rex has parted with captain d4v41 and Jinggg, two Masters Toronto winners, after an early exit at Champions 2026. With its VCT Pacific partner place secure, the Singapore organisation is rebuilding by choice as free agency opens to every region.

Paper Rex has broken up the core of its VALORANT roster. The Singapore organisation is parting with its captain and one of its best-known players as the 2027 season approaches. d4v41 had been with Paper Rex since its founding in 2020. He played first on its CS:GO roster, then moved with the team to VALORANT. Jinggg joined on 28 September 2021.

Neither player has named a destination. In the farewell video Paper Rex released, d4v41 said he was moving to a new team. Jinggg wrote on X that he was excited about what comes next. d4v41 also asked fans to keep supporting the organisation after both have gone.

The split follows a season that faded at the end. Paper Rex were runners-up at both Masters Santiago and Masters London earlier in 2026. At Champions in Shanghai, they lost 2-0 to LOUD in the upper-bracket quarter-finals on 7 October. A 2-1 defeat to T1 in lower-bracket round one ended their run on 9 October. The event carried a $2,250,000 prize pool. LOUD went on to beat Team Vitality in the final.

The pair leave with a long record together. Jinggg helped Paper Rex to second place at Masters Copenhagen 2022. He was also part of the run to the Champions 2023 final, where the team were runners-up. Liquipedia lists both players in the line-up that won VCT 2025 Masters Toronto.

The changes are not forced by the league. The organisation is owned by IMPLS Entertainment Pte Ltd. Riot has cut the number of partner teams in each region from ten to eight for 2027–28. That leaves 32 across the four regions.

The Pacific format rewards that security. The eight partners receive seeded places at Kickoff in January 2027. Four further places go to teams that come through open qualifiers. Paper Rex can therefore reshape its roster without needing to qualify.

Two Masters winners on the open market could matter well beyond the Pacific. EMEA’s eight partners for 2027 are Fnatic, BBL Esports, FUT Esports, Team Heretics, Team Liquid, Gentle Mates, Karmine Corp and Team Vitality. Under Riot’s open qualifier rules, most regions require three of a team’s five players to come from that region. Teams must also keep three of five players between events to carry their progress forward. Those limits will frame how far any club can rebuild around new signings.

Khalish has been part of Paper Rex since our founding in 2020, starting first on our CS:GO Roster and transitioning with the team to VALORANT. We'll always remember the laughs, the op shots, and every achievement through the years.

From everyone at Paper Rex, we wish @d4v41vlr… pic.twitter.com/UgWKD4QfOj

Later in November, open qualifiers get under way. The season’s first Masters event follows in February 2027.

#4281. Best Netflix games available right now - From Into the Breach to Red Dead Redemption

Netflix isn't just a place to watch movies and TV episodes - it's also a great place for gamers to discover new forms of entertainment, with a large library of games from many different developers and genres.

There are numerous hours of fun to be had on Netflix for gamers, from action to puzzle games. On the next pages, you can find a list we compiled after carefully considering all the available games and narrowing them down to give you the top 10 best Netflix games at the moment. How to find and install Netflix Games If you don't have it already, go ahead and download the Netflix app on your device. Keep in mind that you need to have an active Netflix subscription for this.

Now, let's get on with the list of best Netflix games at the moment.

If you don't know anything about the Football Manager franchise, you must be either living under a rock or you just don't like football. But if you do like football and simulation games, then this is a no-brainer.

Become a club manager and take everything under your control, from tactics and transfers to team talks, scouting, and pretty much anything else that you can imagine.

You can start your career at any club in the world, as it supports every league and has real players. As I said, this game is a must if you are looking for a football simulation experience.

Download now! Football Manager 26 Mobile

You already know about Bloons TD 6 from our previous articles, such as Bloons TD 6 tier list and best towers to carry your rounds. In this Netflix game, you benefit from hundreds of configurations and upgrades, so feel free to read all the guides we've created to help you on that journey.

Aside from that, what you need to know about this game is that it's wild. You have a tower defence type of game where things get increasingly more difficult. Towards the last levels, some players even reported crashes because of how crazy the battles turned out.

It's one of the most fun and entertaining tower defence games out there, and easily one of the best games Netflix has to offer.

Oxenfree is a story-driven adventure game with elements of mystery and suspense, sprinkled with paranormal elements.

The story follows a group of teenagers as they face the repercussions of opening a ghostly portal on an abandoned island, while out partying one night. It's also got a smart chat system that lets players have a major impact on the tale's action and conclusion.

New graphics, a remixed soundtrack, a new epilogue, mysteries, and branching story paths can all be found in Oxenfree: Netflix Edition, which was published on September 24th, 2022. If you are interested in this title, here's a link to our full review of Oxenfree, where we get into specifics.

Before Your Eyes is a game with a major focus on storytelling and beauty. The actual story is a little dark at its core, but the way it is presented is far from it.

It gives players the opportunity to immerse themselves in an individual's life, as they journey across the River Styx and into the afterlife. That is as dark as it appears, but it has its beauty.

Before Your Eyes has innovative gameplay with real-time tracking of the player's eye movements and blinking to make choices that impact the outcome of the story. It's not something we typically see in your run-of-the-mill mobile game.

Krispee Street is an adorably designed hidden object game that is exclusively accessible to Netflix members. This title draws inspiration from a well-known webcomic, and its graphics don't shy away from showing that. It's really well done.

As a player, you'll have to figure out puzzles and discover well-hidden objects, and while it might sound like a piece of cake at first, it really isn't. Oh, and it also has a certain narrative that it manages to tell between the puzzles and hidden object games. It's really good, and a nice break from the classical, realistic hidden object game we're used to.

As a kid, you've probably dreamed of defending the Earth from various calamities or invasions and being a hero in the end. Well, Into the Breach will make your childhood dream finally come true. You're the last line of defence against the overgrown bug-like aliens that can crush a building without much effort. However, humanity has advanced, and we have huge mechs and other weapons of destruction because we humans are great at finding the best way to kill each other.

Fighting is done on an 8x8 grid that's similar to chess, with turn-based combat. As terrain can shift and create huge holes in the ground, it can be tricky to avoid them while facing aliens. Therefore, careful planning is essential to win every round, no matter what the end goal is. That's the only way to turn terrain shifts to your advantage, as gravity works on your adversaries as well.

Storyteller is a hit game unlike any other. It starts off pretty slow, with just a couple of prompts, but soon enough you will find yourself in a story unlike any other. The game is available on Steam as well, which is where it was first popularised.

The best part about Storyteller is not the fact that it's sort of a build-your-own-story kind of game, but rather its unique take on it. You will be in charge of making a plot for each prompt you're given, and sometimes these plots have a twist. Literally. It's one of the best Netflix games ever released, and you shouldn't skip it.

Red Dead Redemption likely needs no introduction, though we should take a moment to appreciate how far mobile has come before we get to that. The fact that we can now carry an incredibly complex and detailed open-world shooter like this in our pockets shows the leaps in technology since the game first released way back in 2010.

If you're somehow unfamiliar, it takes place in the Wild West and follows John Marston as he hunts down the surviving members of his old gang. Why? The federal government has taken his family and won't give them back until the job is done. Yeah, it's pretty heavy stuff and is a wonderfully told story. In some ways, I'd argue, it's better than its successor, Red Dead 2. I appreciate that’s a contentious statement, of course.

But it's not all gloomy stuff. Thanks to the open-world nature of it all, there's plenty of twisted fun to be had with tying people to train tracks and waiting for the next locomotive to roll through. Or if you don’t want to act like a Looney Tunes villain, you can swagger into a saloon, find a comfortable corner, and play poker for hours instead. It’s good fun either way.

Download now! Red Dead Redemption NETFLIX

Death might not be the happiest topic in the world, but that doesn't mean it can't provide some level of catharsis when handled well. Spiritfarer takes this complex life event and somehow manages to turn it into a cosy management RPG.

You play as a ferrymaster tasked with guiding the recently passed to the afterlife. It's not a simple case of starting the engines and sailing across to the other side, though. The spirits you encounter are somewhat restless, and you'll need to care for them as they make their final voyage. That means getting to know them and their needs, which makes for an incredibly emotional final goodbye. Still, it's that bittersweet variety of sadness where you'll be pleased you took the plunge.

Aside from chatting to Spiritfarer's lovable cast, you'll also busy yourself with fishing, crafting, mining, farming, and all manner of other things. Just because your destination is a fairly morbid one, it doesn't mean that everyday tasks can fall by the wayside, you see. They're still important and in many ways key to the relaxing vibe Spiritfarer offers.

Inspired by Black Mirror mastermind Charlie Brooker's obsession with keeping a Tamagotchi alive in his youth, Thronglets is a virtual pet sim that tasks you with helping the Throng thrive. They'll hatch from eggs before relying on you for food and entertainment. Do all those things, and you'll have an adorable little army (?). Just don't set them all on fire, alright? The Lisbon event overlapped with PGL Masters Bucharest and finished less than a day before IEM Beijing began.

After the win over 9z, the team’s points already looked sufficient, according to TYLOO coach WeiJie ‘zhokiNg’ Zhong. By that stage, they had no choice but to play the Retake event. Before IEM Beijing, he also spoke about Dongkai ‘Jee’ Ji’s recovery and the problems the team has faced this season.

Europe holds 18 of the 32 Singapore invitations, one more than it had at Cologne. The six highest-ranked eligible European teams in the 2 November standings go straight into Stage 3.

The fight for the final European spot went to the last weekend. The European VRS now places 100 Thieves 18th. Elsewhere, HOTU finished second at GLuck Moscow Cyber Games.

That was bad news for fnatic. Before the final, they sat 18th in Europe with no matches left. Their only route in was a 100 Thieves defeat and recalculated standings falling their way. Neither happened.

#4279. Starsand Island is a life and farming sim that isn't gacha, and it's out next week

Starsand Island officially has an Early Access release date, and it sounds like it won't stay there for years.

Though it may seem like we just had a big life sim release in Heartopia, 2026 actually has more than one highly-anticipated release in that particular subgenre of cozy game. The next big one on the horizon is Starsand Island, the life and farming sim from Seed Sparkle Lab.

The game has been gaining momentum since the launch of a demo in October last year, but the developer never quite managed to commit to a date for its debut title. Until now.

Seed Sparkle Lab announced today that Starsand Island will enter Early Access on February 11, which is only a bit over one week from now. This goes for Steam and the Xbox Preview Program version.

The developer said to expect a fairly short Early Access run, as the full launch is expected in the summer of this year. When the full release arrives, the game will also make the jump to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series, as well as Switch 2.

The full release is also expected to bring Steam Deck support and introduce the multiplayer mode, which will not be available during Early Access

Starsand Island has something of a unique look compared to other games in the subgenre. The storybook, anime-inspired aesthetics are popular in the realm of gacha games, of course. However, seeing as this particular game isn’t gacha, being a premium product means it’s going to offer something free-to-play games aren’t designed to.

Speaking of which, the game will be available in two editions: Standard and Deluxe, with the latter including Romanticism-inspired outfits, furniture, and other customisation items. If you buy either during launch, you’ll also get a Chinese New Year bonus with even more outfits and furniture.

On top of the usual systems of farming, mining, and making friends with adorable characters (and animals), the game also has combat that pits you against ancient guardians. You can, of course, also build a home in it, and decorate it to your heart's content.

Seed Sparkle Lab says you can expect about 100 hours of content in the Early Access launch build, and more features will arrive over the course of the next six or so months, including a crossover event with My Time At Portia.

You can look forward to more Starsand Island coverage from us in the near future. Until then, you can get started by planning who you’re going to date now.

#4278. Ahead of the Game - My Tiny Shop: Relaxing Decor is sticking items in small dioramas, and very relaxing indeed

It's all about keeping everything in its place in this week's Ahead of the Game series, where we tell you about a new mobile endeavour that's playable in one form or another despite its unofficial launch.

I'm starting off the month of November with plenty of cosy vibes as we head into the holiday season, and My Tiny Shop: Relaxing Decor is what's caught my eye this week. It's not only just because the word "relaxing" is already there in the title, but also because it's got a cute goat shopkeeper with swirly glasses as its app icon - and when it comes to the elements in a video game that make me pay attention, I'm very, very shallow.

I love the aesthetics right from the get-go, as the visuals have plenty of soft edges and that charming, hand-drawn feel. As for the gameplay itself, it actually kind of reminds me of the sticker albums I used to collect when I was a kid - I think these sticker-based scenes are becoming a trend nowadays too.

Essentially, you'll need to open a box filled with decorations and then "stick" them onto an empty scene in front of you. Each item has its own rightful place, and you can get hints as to where they're supposed to go based on their outline. There's a combo meter that dwindles down to motivate you to keep sticking, and while the larger items like pieces of furniture are easy enough to spot, the tinier things like random paintbrushes are much more challenging to place.

Eventually, figuring out where something goes gets trickier and trickier the more cluttered the space becomes, as the outlines tend to get buried under what's already there. If you do get stuck, you can opt for combo boosters and hints (which you can get more of by watching ads) to help you out, and when it's all done, you're rewarded by this lovely little scene coming to life before you.

The anthropomorphic animals in the diorama will move and tell a tiny story in that snapshot in time, which is just too wholesome not to marvel at.

Outside of the puzzle stages, you can use the resources you've earned to unlock decor for your own little shop. Whatever you place in your shop isn't just for show - these actually earn you some money periodically, so it's worth collecting these cosmetics to make your own shop thrive. So, how do you play My Tiny Shop: Relaxing Decor? Currently in early access on Google Play, this charming little gem is free to try, but with ads. I didn't feel like they were particularly intrusive, mainly because you get a countdown warning when ads are about to pop up. And I think it's pretty thoughtful of the devs, just so you're not randomly interrupted when you're sticking a particularly tricky little bottle on a desk.

Download now! My Tiny Shop: Relaxing Decor

#4277. The Video Games And More You Should Play This Weekend – October 16, 2026

Welcome to spooky month where lawns suddenly grow giant skeletons, it's cold enough for a hoodie, the remakes of Resident Evil 2, 3, and 4 released on Switch 2, and we're all prepping to hunker down for Winter. And Grand Theft Auto VI.

We're still in the thick of new release season which, fun fact, used to just be the month of November. But now it starts in August and ends in March, give or take a few weeks.

Before we get to our regularly scheduled weekend recommendations, though, here are some of the biggest Game Informer stories of the week.

It has been a long wait for a brand new Castlevania game, and frankly, I think Belmont's Curse has been worth the time spent in the queue. Charles Harte agrees, as he wrote in his review, "Belmont's Curse is a strong reminder of why the Castlevania series is so influential, with a rich world, tense combat, and a map chock-full of secrets. While this latest entry certainly pays homage to the Castlevanias of yore, it also breathes fresh life into the franchise, making me excited for its future. Castlevania is back, and between Rose Belmont and Evil Empire, it's in great hands."

The game comes from the team behind Dead Cells, a game heavily influenced by Castlevania to begin with, and the result shows how great a fit the team and franchise is. Controlling Rose Belmont feels great, the world is big and fun to explore without being overbearing, and beating each boss is a rewarding challenge. I often feel one mark of a good game for me is if it keeps me up past my bedtime, and Belmont's Curse is, unfortunately, doing a great job of making me feel tired all day. But that's a good thing.

The short pitch for Silver Pines is that it is a Metroid-inspired game crossed with a Silent Hill game. That's a good hook on its own, but what makes it stand out (at least in the limited time I have so far spent with it), is its animation. I don't know that it was actually rotoscoped (think the original 1989 Prince of Persia), but it feels like it was, which makes it look great and lends it an intentional level of uncanny valley that aids the creepy atmosphere. Throw in a dash of Twin Peaks energy, and you end up with something that feels unique against a sea of comparable (but often well-designed) Metroid-inspired games.

Just Dance is an frequent tradition in my household. We don't play it every year, but I was eager to check out Decades of Hits because of its included soundtrack. Just Dance generally leans on contemporary music and as a dad facing down his forties (who is still very cool, right? Right?!) I appreciate the chance to learn about recent pop hits and make a fool of myself in front of my family, but I like how musically diverse this entry is.

You have Sabrina Carpenter, Chappell Roan, and Olivia Rodrigo songs (which I adore), but you also get ABBA, Spice Girls, No Doubt, Daft Punk, Britney Spears, Sum 41, TLC, Gorillaz, Run DMC, Billy Joel, and Elton John among many others.

Also, in recent years, Just Dance has started its own tradition of including at least one shockingly impressive stop-motion animated sequence. I am not sure what executive at Ubisoft is accidentally approving the budget for the continued creation of these types of videos, but I hope they never notice because they're great.

You really can’t go wrong with any Jackbox game. Sure, there are some occasional duds in the packages, but there are always at least one or two super fun games that are always worth returning to. 12 is out this week and includes a game about sorting trivia questions into the right categories at high speed, one where you try to make the most ridiculous greeting card, a game encouraging silly debates, one that identifies connections among everyone playing, and finally Hyperface, where you manipulate selfies.

After an earlier release on VR platforms, the rhythm game Maestro recently made its way onto Switch and Switch 2, including a physical game cartridge launch. If you've always secretly loved the idea of stepping up onto the podium for a try at the conductor's gig, it's one worth tracking down. The game includes a number of classical hits from the likes of Beethoven, Vivaldi, and Tchaikovsky, but there's also the chance to play more contemporary tracks like those you'd hear in Star Wars or Game of Thrones. With Joy-Cons in hand, you'll keep the tempo, cue in musicians, adjust dynamics, and more. The accompanying visuals and "storytelling" aren't going to blow your mind, but the included music is hard to beat, and with occasional exceptions where the game misread my motions, I found the motion-tracking mostly up to the task of nailing the fantasy.

If you spent hours playing the early Toy Story games, then the retro compilation masters at Digital Eclipse have something for you in the form of Toy Story: Retro Roundup. On top of Toy Story, Toy Story 2: Buzz Lightyear to the Rescue, Toy Story 2, Buzz Lightyear of Star Command, and Toy Story Racer (including multiple versions of many of these), you can also get your hands on the 1998 A Bug's Life game. It may not have the breadth of extra content of something like Digital Eclipse's Atari 50 or Tetris Forever, but it's a fun stroll down memory lane with some behind-the-scenes interviews and materials. Alongside this retro collection, there's also the separate Toy Story 3 Complete Edition, also released by Digital Eclipse this week.

Kingdom Hearts Collection [I~III] – yes, that’s really what it’s called – is out on Nintendo Switch 2, and after spending some time with it, man, it feels right at home on the console. This collection includes Kingdom Hearts HD 1.5 +2.5 ReMix (which itself includes a bunch of Kingdom Hearts games, including 1 and 2), Kingdom Hearts HD 2.8 Final Chapter Prologue, and Kingdom Hearts III + Re Mind DLC. Basically, it has everything you need to catch up on the Kingdom Hearts saga before Kingdom Hearts IV launches next year.

As for actually playing these games, they feel amazing on Switch 2, courtesy of HD resolutions, on handheld and docked, and 60 FPS gameplay. I don’t know why exactly, but playing the Kingdom Hearts series on Switch 2 just feels right. It probably has something to do with just how many of these games were Nintendo console originals. Nonetheless, if you’re new to Kingdom Hearts or looking for a new place to tear up while "Dearly Beloved" plays, this Switch 2 collection will satisfy your needs.

This new standalone version of Forest Shuffle does more than transplant the theming into the Smoky Mountains of North America. It has also allowed its creators to refine balance, add new elements (like an intriguing new water/river terrain), create a more vibrant and visually beautiful presentation, and overall, up the value and playability of the game across the board. In short, it's what I think is the best version of an already very good game.

For newcomers, the Forest Shuffle formula is a card game that involves a mix of card hand management and tableau-building, as you slowly play out a forest scene onto the table, filled with unique trees, animals, and plants, and gathering points for the types and variety of things living in your woods. It's an approachable and visually enchanting game that still offers plenty of strategic depth as you plan out the shape and potential of your nature scene, all while planning against the impending arrival of winter.

#4276. Death Stranding Odradek shows us how Kojima's hit series might work on mobile

Death Stranding is, for better or for worse, a quintessentially Kojima game. And it's found a lot of success on virtually every platform, including on mobile. But a newly released prototype app exclusive to a recent gallery could show how else the franchise works on mobile, as Death Stranding Odradek hits iOS and Android!

Death Stranding Odradek allows visitors to the Azabudai Hills Gallery, which is hosting the 10th anniversary exhibition for Kojima Productions, to complete a delivery mission and experience the world of Death Stranding through AR. Odradek is named for the device worn on Sam's back in Death Stranding, which provides you with in-game information about the terrain and world around you, as well as warning of the presence of dangerous BTs.

And it wouldn't be out of the question for it to see a wider release either, as Kojima was very vocal about seeing Death Stranding as a new genre in and of itself, a so-called 'strand game' where multiplayer and social gameplay was vital to progression. And while Odradek offers what seems to be mainly a single-player experience, it's an interesting prototype nonetheless.

I'd certainly be curious to see a full-fledged version of the game, which offers a similar experience to Death Stranding itself. Certainly, with walking and movement being such a core part of the experience, as well as social elements, it could make for a thinking-man's Pokémon Go.

Still, while Odradek is an exciting concept for a game, you may be feeling something a little goofier and more fun that you can play with friends. If so, why not check out our review of Jackbox Party Pack 12 for our thoughts on the latest entry in the series?

#4275. Nioh 3 launches, immediately becomes the most played Nioh ever on Steam

Just a few hours after launch, Nioh 3 is already the biggest release in series history on Steam.

It sounds like Koei Tecmo’s decision to finally release a Nioh game on PC day-and-date with PlayStation has paid off. The highly-anticipated Nioh 3 has gone live across both platforms, a first for a series that typically spends its initial release months as a console exclusive.

On Steam, and despite having only been available for just a few hours, the game has broken series records, and it continues to climb.

At the time of writing, Nioh 3 has peaked at 42,822 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), and the number keeps going up. Because it’s in the middle of day in Europe and everyone is at work, it’s entirely possible - if not likely - that this figure will get much higher. A weekend bump is also possible, as we’ve seen with several recent releases.

As it stands, the current peak concurrent is enough to get the game in Steam’s top 20 most played games.

This already puts it ahead of all other Nioh games on Steam. The original Nioh peaked at 10,649 when it released in November, 2017. Nioh 2 fared much better, peaking at 41,325 concurrent players in February, 2021.

Of course, you could see that success coming a mile away. The game is currently number one worldwide in Steam’s list of top sellers. This is a jump of 46 positions, for a total of three weeks Nioh 3 has spent in that list.

There are many reasons as to why Nioh 3 has done as well as it has. Word of mouth coming off last year’s PS5-exclusive demo, and the more positive coverage that followed since are just two.

Just last week, Team Ninja released a pretty generous demo across both platforms, which has been well received by players, and likely contributed to sales, in no small part because progress in the demo carries over to the full game.

Critical reviews have been incredibly positive, too. We awarded the game four out of five stars, calling it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.” It will be interesting to see what number the highest peak concurrent actually settles on over the weekend.

Until then, if you’re jumping in yourself, our Nioh 3 guides are essential reading. Start off with these useful and actually informative gameplay tips, and don’t start playing until you’ve changed these settings. #4274. 10 Pokémon That Are More Powerful Than Their Evolution

Laurence Wall is a Contributor at DualShockers who has been writing professionally since 2022 and covering games since 2023. He primarily writes guides and lists, with a focus on indie games, RPGs, ARPGs, Soulslikes, MMOs, card games, boss fights, and detailed tutorials.

Pokémon that are more powerful than their evolution? I mean, that sounds impossible, right? Isn’t the point of evolution to make a Pokémon more powerful, giving it more stats, new types and moves, and all that jazz? Well, yes, on paper. But Pokémon isn’t that simple.

For example, in Generation 5, a new hold item changed the competitive landscape for good. This item is called Eviolite, and it boosts a Pokémon's defence and special defence by 50% as long as that Pokémon hasn’t fully evolved. While Pokémon do get a good chunk of stats from evolving, that's rarely even close to 50%!

Who wouldn't want a Fox for a pet? This also goes for Pokemon. But these Pokemon aren't just cute, they'll burn you to cinders too!

It’s hard to put into words how powerful this item is, but it's safe to say it breathed new life into Pokémon that often didn’t really see the light of day. So let’s go over a few Pokémon that got to shine, some with the Eviolite, and some on their own merit!

I had to give Pikachu a bit of a shout-out here, and not because of Ash’s freakishly powerful Pikachu in the Anime. No. While Pikachu doesn’t see much play in the main games, or even competitively, that doesn’t mean it can’t be powerful under the right conditions.

Pikachu has its own special held item, the Light Ball, which doubles its offensive stats. While most people would prefer Raichu, Pikachu has a decent Speed stat, letting it outspeed many opponents. Plus, with its unique move Volt Tackle, it can KO many Pokémon with a single hit.

You’ll just have to hope you don’t get hit, because Pikachu's defences are paper thin!

Scyther is a really interesting case. Right now, Scyther has 2 evolutions: Scizor and Kleavor. Generally, when a Pokémon evolves, it gains a healthy chunk of base stats, but Scyther is completely different.

Scyther already has a great Base Stat Total of 500, so instead of getting even more stats, it changes its type, going from Bug/Flying to Bug/Steel or Bug/Rock. And while these evolutions are great, Scyther doesn’t actually need them to be strong.

Scyther doesn’t even need Eviolite because of its massive Attack and Speed. In this case, we can use a Choice Scarf or a Choice Band to capitalise on those base stats, or give it a Sash and aim for a sweep with Swords Dance. Scyther has plenty of options and shows just how versatile it really is.

Misdreavus received its evolution in Generation 4, evolving into Mismagius. This gave it a nice buff, with a good chunk of extra Special Attack and Speed, so it can deal some real damage.

The thing is, regular Misdreavus doesn’t actually have bad stats. In fact, its defences are pretty solid. Now equip this little ghost with an Eviolite, and now you have something interesting. While you won’t be throwing out any Shadow Balls with this, you can instead use moves like Perish Song and Pain Split to stall your opponents out.

Or use their might against them with moves like Foul Play, and burn them down with Will-O-Wisp. You’ll have them running away in fear in no time!

Electivire is another one of these strange cases where a Pokemon loses stats upon evolving. While it gains a higher Base Stat Total, mainly from its extra Attack, it actually loses Speed. The great thing about Electabuzz is that it already has a really fantastic BST of 490!

Yep, you know what that means! It’s a brilliant candidate for the Eviolite. So here, instead of using physical attacks, it’s best to use some of Electabuzz’s more interesting support moves. With only one weakness, you can tank a lot of hits with Follow Me while baiting the opponent with Taunt.

Then, when another Pokemon comes in, you can use Volt Switch to pivot while dealing a good chunk of damage with Electabuzz’s already great special attack stat.

I don’t think I was the only one who was a little bit underwhelmed when Rhyperior was released in the fourth Generation. This isn’t to say it’s a bad Pokemon; its design is just a little bit weird, especially compared to Rhydon, which is just so iconic.

The thing is, Rhyperior gets Solid Rock, which helps it avoid being one-shot by special Water and Grass moves. So, to counter that, it makes sense to run an Eviolite to massively boost Rhydon’s survivability.

Then we can make use of Rhydon’s amazing attack stat to throw out powerful Stone Edges and Earthquakes. And if you were worried about Rhydon not making much of an impact, it also gets access to Stealth Rock for guaranteed chip damage when your opponents switch too often!

Duosion often gets massively overlooked. You know it’s just one of the middle-stage Pokémon that isn’t very unique, just looking like a transition stage to get to the next point. And Reuniclus, naturally, is much more visually interesting.

But one funny thing is that Duosion and Reuniclus have the exact same Special Attack stat. Yep, in terms of their offensive potential, they’re equal! Now, with the defensive boost Eviolite gives alongside Magic Guard, you can massively skyrocket Duosion's offensive and defensive capabilities with Calm Mind.

Pair this with stalling moves like Recover and Acid Armour to cover its normal defence, and you can ramp up to deal serious damage with Stored Power, which uses all your stat boosts for insane damage!

Chansey and Blissey are known for having the biggest HP pools in the games, and for giving out a ton of EXP, of course! But what advantage does Blissey actually have over Chansey?

Well, when it evolves, Blissey gets a good amount of Special Attack. But the thing is, you’re never going to use these Pokémon as attackers! They’re always going to be for healing and stalling. So, instead, Chansey benefits so much more from an Eviolite, making it less likely to faint from a powerful physical attack.

Then you can use Chansey to set up Stealth Rock and Thunder Wave, or even chip the opponents down with Seismic Toss. With Soft-Boiled for healing, if your opponents don’t have many physical attackers, Chansey can be a real pain to take down!

A good while back, when we were kids in school, I heard a strange strategy called F.E.A.R floating around. And yes, I was royally schooled when a friend used it against me. This little Acronym stands for Focus Sash, Endeavor, Quick Attack, Rattata, and if your opponent doesn’t know how it works, it can take out the most powerful Pokémon around.

Of course, this only works once, right? Well, how about if there was a better version? Meet our Level 1 Aron. Here, you won’t need Focus Sash because Aron has Sturdy as its ability, and instead of Quick Attack, you’ll use Sandstorm for chip damage.

When Aron is reduced to 1 HP, use Endeavor to match your HP with the opponent's. Then the Shell Bell Aron is holding activates, restoring it to full health, while Sandstorm takes out the opponent. You’re free to keep abusing this loop until your opponent runs out of Pokémon … or until they figure out the strategy.

This is a bit of a meme, to be honest, and any decent trainer will immediately know how to counter it, but it shows how weak Pokémon can actually be strong under the right conditions!

Dusclops is pretty similar to Chansey in that it evolves, but the evolution doesn’t do much! Upon evolution, Dusknoir gets a decent buff to its Attack and Speed stats, but like with Blissey, you wouldn’t really run this Pokémon as a physical attacker. There are just better options available.

So, since Dusclops already has great base defensive stats, an Eviolite makes so much more sense, turning it into an absolute wall! Ghost is a great defensive type, so Dusclops can make great use of stalling tactics with Toxic/Will-O-Wisp and Pain Split.

Dusclops also works well as a Trick Room setter, thanks to its low speed, letting other slow Pokémon on your team shine. And if you need damage, Night Shade is a great way to guarantee it, no matter your opponent's stats! While Dusknoir is cool, Dusclops does everything so much better.

Porygon has a great story. It starts in Generation 1 as an extremely hard-to-obtain Pokémon, evolves in Generation 2, and becomes corrupted in its final stage in Generation 4. The whole evolution line is great.

That's why I love Porygon2 so much. So with Porygon-Z, it’s obviously used as a special-attacking sweeper. With a base Special Attack of 135, what else would it be used for? But the thing is, to gain this power, it loses a lot of its bulk, about 20 points from Defence and Special Defence.

And of course, you know what it’s time for! Eviolite! A lot of the previous Pokemon on this list struggle with their stats. They might have great defences but low HP or vice versa, which makes them struggle against certain matchups. With Eviolite, Porygon2 has ridiculously high defences and a ton of HP! Best of both worlds!

First off, we get Recover to help sustain. Then we add Thunder Wave to slow and stall. Then add a strong coverage move like Ice Beam to take advantage of Porygon2’s great special attack. Finally, you have a 4th slot for whatever you want: Protect, Foul Play, Trick Room, whatever you want!

It’s funny, because Porygon2 is a Pokémon you would never expect to be such a tank, and honestly, that’s why it’s so iconic.

Everybody loves Pokémon, but what about ones that roamed the planet in prehistoric times? This list is all about every dinosaur pokémon!

A dark detective thriller where folklore is real, violence is chilling, and every choice has consequences.

#4270. Silver Palace, the Belle Époque-style ARPG, sets release date for this winter

With so many ARPGs on storefronts these days, a new one can seem a little redundant. But as the debut entry in the genre from Elementa Games, Silver Palace is already shaping up to be an exciting new release. And soon you'll be able to judge for yourself, as Silver Palace is confirmed to land on December 14th for iOS and Android!

Inspired by a mix of Victorian and Belle Époque fashion, Silver Palace is set in a sprawling metropolis called Silvernia, which is undergoing an industrial revolution powered by... you guessed it: Silverium. This means magic and technology intertwine, with brawling melee action accompanied by high-calibre weaponry.

Having played Silver Palace myself, I feel confident in saying that its combat and exploration were extremely engaging. Of course, that was only a vertical slice of everything that's available, so the whole game may hold up very differently.

But overall, for Elementa, Silver Palace is shaping up to be an exciting debut, with an interesting world and exciting gameplay. So keep your eyes peeled for when Silver Palace lands December 14th, and dive into the action and intrigue of Silvernia!

In the meantime, if you're looking for other ARPGs to hone your skills, then we've got you covered. No need to sift through the app stores when you can just check out our list of the best mobile games of 2026 (so far) to see some choice picks you can play right now on your smartphone!

#4269. Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.0 brings a new world, and a Fortnite collaboration

Honkai: Star Rail's next major update introduces a whole new planet to the RPG, and way more besides.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a big Honkai: Star Rail Special Program. We’ve been waiting for this one for a couple of weeks now thanks to a delay, but the developer has finally delivered all the news on Version 4.0, which will arrive February 13.

The upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason. Aha's Planarcadia is the big new world headlining Version 4.0.

Planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations. In-universe, however, it was born out of the pages of an art canvas, and it’s a world where pleasure is king.

The squad’s host in this chapter is Madam Pearl, who will oversee the the Astral Express’ return to the place where they first began their journey. Duomension City is where you’re going to land, and meet the creatures that dwell in this world.

The imagenae of Planarcadia require attention to survive, and they feed off people’s Wishpower. If they don’t get any attention, they perish, which does tie into the general themes of the place. Duomension City has other interesting locations that you’re going to visit, such as the Graphia Academy art school, the commercial district of Dovebrook, and a few other places hidden behind mysterious entrances.

The Phantasmoon Games is another highlight of Planarcadia, a competitive spectacle where you’ll have a chance to compete to become Aeon for a Minute. If you make it to the final stages, you may earn an audience with The Laughter.

Much like the world where the games take place, the whole point of the competition is to attract the most attention, so rules are a bit loose as to how you manage to do that. The event will bring together several of the game’s factions, though not everyone is there for the competition.

As you explore Planarcadia, if you have characters on your team who are on the newly-playable Path of Elation, you’ll earn Punchlines. The more you accumulate, the closer you get to catching Aha’s attention, which triggers Aha Instant.

Version 4.0 introduces two new 5-Star characters to Honkai: Star Rail. General Yao Guang (Madam Yao) is one, a Seer Strategist from the Xianzhou Alliance's Yuque. If you’ve been playing the game, you may already be familiar with her voice, as she's previously been in touch with our heroes via radio link. But V4.0 marks her first on-screen appearance, as well as her playable debut.

General Yao Guang is a Physical character on the Path of Elation whose specialty is using Weal and Woe Lots in battle, which she uses to increase Elation for allies, and grant everyone Punchline any time she uses a Skill. If an Aha Instant is triggered, she casts Woe Lots, which debuff enemies, causing them to take increased damage, all while regenerating Skill Points for the rest of the team.

Her aptly named Certified Banger buff adds one extra instance of Elation to teammates’ attacks. And her Ultimate grants the team Punchline, and triggers an extra Aha Instant.

The other new arrival is likewise a Path of Elation devotee. Sparxie is a suspiciously familiar streamer who uses her influencer skills in combat. When she fights, she turns the fight into a battle for attention, as she forces enemies to engage in a race for upvotes.

When you consume Skill Points, Sparxie will get gifts, which in turn cause her to regenerate Skill Points and Punchlines for the team. You can continue doing this to increase your damage. When Aha Instant is triggered, Sparxie unleashes a lucky draw that deals damage to enemies with each bounce.

She also benefits from the Certified Banger state, which causes the gifs she receives to deal more Elation damage to a random enemy target. Her Ultimate also deals more Elation damage.

Version 4.0 will see a few re-runs, too. Black Swan, Evernight, and Hysilens will be part of the first half's Warp events. The second half will see the return of Sparkle, Cerydra, and Rappa — that's right, HoYoverse have finally remembered Rappa exists, after one of the longest rerun waits in the game's history! Both Black Swan and Sparkle are getting a few tweaks to their kit with this version, too, so the timing works.

If you log in after launch, you’ll get 20 free pulls and a new free outfit for Ruan Mei. If you play while the Yao Guang fortune event is active, you could earn 1,600 Stellar Jades. You can also expect a free 5-Star character selector to arrive at some point after launch, giving you a free choice between popular (but admittedly a bit old for the meta these days) limited-banner characters Jing Yuan, Kafka, Dan Heng • Imbibitor Lunae, Jingliu, Sparkle, Acheron, and Aventurine.

Finally, the other major news is a Fortnite collaboration. Starting February 26, Kafka and Blade will join Epic’s battle royale shooter. On that day, you’ll find skins of the two Stellaron Hunters in the Fortnite Item Shop, and the new outfits are even compatible with Fortnite's LEGO styles. You can also expect other customisation bits like Back Bling, Pickaxe, and more to be part of the package.

If you download the game on the Epic Games Store, and take part in Honkai: Star Rail-themed activities, you’ll also get the Blade character outfit in Fortnite for free. Event schedule and timing will be announced at a later date.

#4268. Nintendo Switch Sports Resort Review - Still In Motion

Originating as a tech demo for the Wii’s motion controls, Nintendo’s Sports series has always found novel and intuitive ways to emulate various athletic endeavors with motion-based video game controllers. Like its predecessors, Switch Sports Resort is a compilation of sports-based minigames built around approachability. Though rightfully known for its enticing multiplayer options, Switch Sports Resort adds new single-player objectives and modes to offer a well-rounded experience for all player counts, making it perhaps the strongest entry in the series to date.

Switch Sports Resort delivers 12 main events to choose from, each with distinct controls, strategies, and rules. Mainstays like bowling, archery, boxing, and golf were my initial destinations to attempt to relive old glories, but newcomers like thumb wrestling, skateboarding, power cruising, and prop plane made me glad for their inclusion.

Skateboarding, power cruising, and prop plane form a new category called leisure sports, which allow for timed exploration of the newly renovated Wuhu Island by land, sea, and sky, respectively. I spent several sessions seeking out landmarks and collecting Spocco Points, the in-game currency used for character customization. And since all the sports’ controls are so intuitive and newcomer-friendly, it was a breeze to jump between activities.

Though they all boil down to moving your arms in something approximating motions you’d make playing the real sport, Nintendo has smartly implemented more variety in its control schemes, all while keeping them easy to pick up. Before the tutorial even explains how to hold the Joy-Con, you can likely accurately guess what the grip and motion will be; even more involved control schemes like basketball and volleyball are easy to remember.

Skateboarding is particularly innovative, as it uses Switch 2’s Joy-Con’s mouse mode to emulate the kick-push of a skater. Meanwhile, prop plane has you holding your Joy-Con like a paper airplane as you fly around blasting balloons and visiting landmarks. However, holding the Joy-Con that way for several minutes inevitably cramped my hand. And though boxing remains one of my favorite sports in the bundle, I needed to retrain my brain, as throwing a punch the correct way doesn’t work with how the game wants you to do it; if I turn my wrist when punching, my character sways instead of attacking.

Playing with friends, both online and in-person, remains the highlight of Switch Sports Resort. The online friend lobby system receives a boost in the form of allowing different sports to take place simultaneously within the same lobby, and when you add in special variants like simultaneous archery, 100-pin bowling, skateboard racing, and prop plane balloon battles, you have a lot of fun options with which to jump in.

Whenever I play solo, the Island Crown is where I spend most of my time. Here, you climb the ranks across nine sports, sometimes with special rulesets, vanquishing NPC opponents until you are the champion. Whether it was taking to increasingly outlandish bowling lanes, windier archery ranges, or simply facing off against more strategic table tennis players, I relished in improving my skills en route to the championship.

Because these minigames are relatively surface level, they have diminishing returns once you reach a certain skill level. While I loved it when my tennis opponents started challenging me to use better angles and my fellow golfers stopped air-mailing their tee shots straight into the trees, higher-skill opponents rarely energized me; instead, sports like bowling that include fun, off-the-wall variants were my favorite ladders to ascend, as they truly put my skills to the test as I was forced to adapt to moving obstacles and ramps. I just wish Nintendo injected more fun twists to keep the experiences fresh.

After completing each activity, you’re awarded Spocco Points, which you use to unlock themed customization elements for your characters. Cartoon-like Sportsmates replace the iconic Mii characters introduced in Wii Sports, but you can still use your Mii if you choose. Though I have fondness for Mii characters, after two entries featuring the more expressive, customizable Sportsmates, I now prefer those character models.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort delivers a capable compilation of quick-hit sports minigames that can be easily enjoyed regardless of how many people are holding Joy-Cons. Though I certainly have my destination sports, there’s not a loser in the bunch. Island Crown mode does a great job expanding the single-player options, but this package’s legs are in its multiplayer experience. And since Switch Sports Resort is chock-full of easily approachable minigames, I can see it becoming a cherished inclusion in the rotation of party mainstays.

#4267. Waframe's new Tau expansion announces launch date for this winter

It seems as if many games nowadays are promising major, paradigm-shifting expansions. We saw it with RuneScape: Reignited, a semi-standalone version of the hit MMORPG, to bring in a new wave of players. But whereas Jagex eventually had to backpedal on their planned spinoff ecosystem, Digital Extremes' new Warframe: Tau expansion looks set to be a true game-changer.

The core selling point of Warframe: Tau is that this is a new, expansive single-player narrative to jump into, that sees the long-dormant Tau sector opened for exploration. The sector itself was already explored in the Old Peace update, but now you'll be able to see what's happened to it in the aeons since.

Tau will also allow you to unlock new versions of fan-favourite cooperative modes, including a new survival mission on the Fornax moon of Perita. You'll also find a brand-new social hub to explore with Manifold 90-BF, with plenty of new characters to meet and secrets to uncover.

All this new space to uncover, including the crime world of Fornax, certainly indicates Warframe: Tau will live up to its game-changing hype. But if you want to judge for yourself, you'll just have to play it when Warframe: Tau lands this December for all platforms!

In the meantime, if you want to take the weight off and relax ahead of such a jam-packed expansion, we've got some suggestions. Why not dig into our list of the best RPGs on Android to see what selections we think are worth playing?
